pyautogui.typewrite("(per CDC "Storage and Handling of Immunobiologics," cdc.gov: an out-of-range reading requires quarantine and documentation, and viability depends on the magnitude and duration of the excursion; vaccines held at inappropriate temperatures should not be administered unless the manufacturer or state health authority confirms they are still safe and effective. This excursion was a modest ~3.4 C overshoot sustained for ~5 hours.)

1. Influenza quadrivalent (FluZone), 40 doses, lot FZ2291 - USABLE (do not discard).
   Reason: Inactivated, aluminum-adjuvanted influenza vaccine tolerates brief excursions above 8 C. At 11.4 C (within the 8-15 C band) for only 5 hours (under the 8-hour limit), it stays within the accepted excursion range. Retain for use, document, and confirm with the manufacturer.

2. Varicella (Varivax), 12 doses, lot VX0847 - DISCARD.
   Reason: VARIVAX is a live, lyophilized vaccine and the most heat-sensitive of the three; it is meant to be stored frozen, not in the refrigerator. These vials were already out of their intended frozen storage and were then warmed to 11.4 C. Under the CDC rule, a live vaccine at inappropriate temperatures should not be administered absent manufacturer clearance, so the correct determination is to discard and restock.

3. Hepatitis B adult (Engerix-B), 25 doses, lot HB5560 - USABLE (do not discard).
   Reason: Inactivated, aluminum-adjuvanted hepatitis B vaccine, like the influenza product, tolerates brief excursions above 8 C. A 5-hour exposure at 11.4 C (at or below 15 C) is within the accepted limit. Retain for use, document, and confirm with the manufacturer.

Actions: Quarantine and label the affected lots "do not use" pending confirmation, record the excursion data (date, duration, max temperature), and confirm each determination with the manufacturer/state immunization program before administration.")
